Native Americans and First Nations people in the United States of America and Canada, respectively, have significantly lower overall rates of cancer than other populations in the United states and Canada, but have significantly higher incidence for cancers of kidney and gallbladder.

Native males and females had a significantly lower incidence for cancer for all sites, and among Native males kidney cancer was found significantly elevated and significantly lower incidence was seen for colon, lung, prostate, and lymphomas and leukemias.

Native males have significantly higher incidence of cancer of the kidney and lower incidence of cancer of colon, lung, prostate and lymphomas and leukemia; Native females have significantly higher incidence for cancer of gall bladder, cervix, kidney, and lower incidence of breast cancer and cancers of colon, uterus, and lymphomas.
